$comment: The aura ramp. SEMANTICS ONLY — no hex values live here. The hexes are
in css/tokens.css (--color-aura-red and siblings) and are joined onto
this map by scripts/generate.mjs, exactly as gems.json is joined. Read
dist/tokens.json for the joined result.
⚠️ THIS IS A RATE MAP. A colour here means a POSITION — how fast a
person's gratitude is circulating — not a medium (that is gems.json)
and not a domain (that is tlds.json). Three palettes; seven, seven and
six; and the hues rhyme because a colour wheel is small. Never present
any two of them as one system.
⚠️ THE SEVENTH IS VIOLET, NOT DIAMOND. This ramp and the gem palette
both have seven stops and they are DIFFERENT SETS: this one carries
indigo and ends at violet; the gems carry no indigo and end at the
unrefracted diamond. The shared count is a coincidence.
⚠️ DISCRETE, NOT CONTINUOUS. colorFor() returns a bucket NAME, so a
person is in exactly one stop and never between two. That is what
makes seven flat tokens the right shape here. The Metta Light — the
gem-order descent named in gems.json — is the continuous one, driven
by a single 0-to-1 scalar. Do not build this one as a gradient.
meaning: Circulation velocity, computed as crossings per month over a rolling window and bucketed server-side.
source: thank.heartbank.org/functions/src/auras/compute.ts — COLOR_BUCKETS is canonical for the thresholds; this file is canonical for the colours.
twoRings: A person carries TWO auras at once — one for Kiitos (gratitude shown) and one for Kiitti (kindness given). Same ramp, two independent positions.

$comment: HOW THE RAMP IS WORN. Extracted from thank.heartbank.org's
aura-avatar component, which stays canonical for the
IMPLEMENTATION; this block is canonical for the INVARIANT.
No values here either — the reference size and base ring width
belong to the consumer. What is pinned here is the shape and the
one property that must not be lost when a second surface renders
an aura.
geometry.innerRing: Kiitos — gratitude shown. A border on the photo circle.
geometry.outerRing: Kiitti — kindness given. Outside the border. A FAMILY avatar carries the outer ring ONLY; a person carries both.
geometry.diameterParity: ⭐ THE INVARIANT, and it is what stops an aura becoming a rank: an avatar's visible total is ALWAYS its declared size plus two base ring widths, whatever the amplitude. A wider ring shrinks the PHOTO; it never grows the avatar. Two people rendered at the same size occupy the same space, so no reading of the geometry makes one of them larger. This is a PROPERTY — remove the enforcer and it still holds, because the arithmetic has nowhere to put the extra width.
geometry.amplitudeIsOptIn: Ring WIDTH carries amplitude only where a surface opts in. The default is width from size alone, so intensity is carried by COLOUR ONLY. Where amplitude is on, each ring is capped as a fraction of size so the photo stays the dominant element.
geometry.honestLimit: ⚠️ Parity bounds the FOOTPRINT, not the comparison. With amplitude shown, two rings side by side still differ visibly in width, and width is still legible as more-or-less. The Zero-Point Game's amplitude seam is NARROWED by this, not closed — that seam remains open and is held by the anti-ranking rules, which are rules and not properties.

$comment: NOT AN EIGHTH STOP. This is the absence of a position, and it
must not be reachable by bucketing — nothing computes it.
noReading.rule: ⛔ A person with no computed aura — never active yet, or a read that FAILED — must NOT be painted at the ramp's floor. Red means measured-and-slow; absence means nothing was measured. Collapsing the two makes the surface assert a fact no computation produced, and it renders the person at their floor to do it.
noReading.whyItMatters: The compute side already honours this on the way IN: a hover at zero counts only while the participant is ACTIVE, because the measure is meant to say 'I keep passing on what I receive' and never 'I hold nothing and do nothing'. A client that paints absence as the floor hands that back.
noReading.treatment: A neutral, NON-CHROMATIC ring that keeps its geometry, so diameter parity is preserved and nothing is painted. Grey — never black or white: each of those goes loud in one theme and vanishes in the other, so the same absence would read as emphatic on a light ground and absent on a dark one. White additionally collides with the diamond gem, a deliberate cool near-white that already means a medium.
noReading.values: Held by the consumer, per this file's no-hex rule. The reference implementation reuses the greys its avatar already uses for the anonymous state, so the vocabulary for 'we are not telling you about this person' is reused rather than invented.

buckets.name: indigo
buckets.note: ⚠️ FOUR SHIPPED SURFACES RENDERED THIS BUCKET IN PINK — members-panel.ts, seed, thank and timelog reached for bg-pink-100/text-pink-400 while the three hex maps said #4f46e5. Pink is reserved by construction for B-Dating and must not appear on a Phase-1 surface. Corrected to indigo. If the reason was that blue-indigo-violet are hard to tell apart at tint weight, the fix is to widen the ramp here, where one change reaches every surface — never to borrow the reserved hue on four of them.

reserved.pink: ABSENT HERE FOR THE SAME REASON IT IS ABSENT FROM THE GEMS — held for B-Dating and romantic contexts. This ramp is where the reservation was actually being violated.

collisions: Both are coincidence, not kinship. Three names, three meanings; do not alias them, or re-tuning one will silently move the others.
